UseCaseDescription:
Prabhix Technologies (https://prabhixtechnologies.com) sends only transactional mail from the verified domain prabhixtechnologies.com in ap-south-1. DKIM for that domain is SUCCESS. We do not send newsletters, promotions, or purchased lists, and there is no bulk-send job.

How often: a message is sent only when a person takes an action. Signup, sign-in codes, and password resets go out once per request. Shop and helpdesk mail goes out when a tenant records a sale, repair, invoice, or replies to a ticket the customer opened. Expected volume is about 500 to 2,000 messages a day at launch, a few messages per active user per day.

Recipient lists: we do not buy, rent, or scrape addresses. An address is stored only when that person registers an account or emails a tenant shared mailbox. Signup keeps the details for 10 minutes and creates the account only after the person enters the emailed code. Staff addresses are added by a tenant administrator for people who work there.

Bounces, complaints, and unsubscribes: SES account suppression is already on for BOUNCE and COMPLAINT. SES events are delivered to an HTTPS webhook whose signature is checked against the Amazon SNS certificate. A hard bounce or complaint suppresses that address immediately and stops further mail to it. Soft bounces are retried with backoff and then suppressed. Security, verification, and billing mail cannot be switched off. Other notifications have a per-user preference in account settings and a link in the message. A support reply is an answer to mail the customer sent, not a list.

Examples we send: (1) Subject "Confirm your Prabhix account", a 6-digit code that expires in 10 minutes, only after the person submits the signup form. (2) Subject "Your Prabhix sign-in code", a one-time sign-in code. (3) Subject "Reset your Prabhix password", a single-use link. (4) A repair shop's message to its own customer about a job that customer brought in.

We are requesting production access so this mail can reach the customer's own address. In the sandbox those addresses are rejected because they are not pre-verified identities.
